The AI Reality

Opportunity. Disruption. Responsibility.

Artificial intelligence is transforming how we work, create, and compete. But progress comes with trade-offs. Understanding both sides is essential to making smarter decisions.

+

The Opportunities

  • Greater productivity
  • Lower operating costs
  • Accelerated innovation
  • Improved decision support
  • Access to powerful new capabilities
!

The Risks

  • Workforce displacement
  • Misinformation and bias
  • Privacy and security concerns
  • Unreliable outputs
  • Overdependence on technology
A balanced approach

Beyond the Hype

The question isn't simply whether AI is good or bad. It's where AI creates meaningful value, where it introduces unacceptable risks, and where human judgment remains essential.

The Nova Forge Perspective

We believe AI should enhance human capability—not replace human accountability. Our approach emphasizes practical applications, responsible implementation, and measurable business value.

STRATEGIC ADVISORY / VENTURE DEVELOPMENT

AeroCordon — Connecting the Pieces of an Emerging Venture

Supporting the advancement of an early-stage defense technology concept through research, technical relationships, capital introductions, and military innovation opportunities.

01 / RESEARCHResearch & IP

DePaul patentability research and intellectual property planning.

02 / TECHNOLOGYTechnology Partners

Technical feasibility and possible integration discussions.

03 / CAPITALCapital Connections

Investor and strategic adviser introductions.

04 / DEFENSEMilitary Opportunities

U.S. Army xTechSearch 10 innovation funding submission.

Stage: Early-stage venture development

The Challenge

Advancing an emerging defense concept required more than a technical idea. The venture needed support across intellectual property research, possible technology relationships, capital access, and pathways to military stakeholders—all while the concept remained in early development.

The Strategic Approach

Help connect the expertise, relationships, and opportunities needed to move the venture forward. Workstreams focused on research and IP, technical discussions, investor introductions, and relevant military innovation programs rather than a conventional marketing launch.

The Advisory Work

  • Supported the DePaul University patent research initiative to inform intellectual property considerations.
  • Helped advance discussions with a potential technology partner about feasibility and integration possibilities.
  • Leveraged professional relationships to facilitate investor and strategic adviser introductions.
  • Contributed to the preparation and submission of an xTechSearch 10 white paper for U.S. Army innovation funding consideration.
  • Worked alongside the founder to prioritize next-stage business development activities.

Progress & Key Takeaway

The venture pursued patentability research, technical conversations, capital introductions, and a military innovation submission. These activities established early-stage pathways, not confirmed funding, deployment, investment, or technical validation.

Key takeaway: Emerging technology ventures move forward by connecting the right expertise, relationships, resources, and opportunities—not simply by defining a product.

Case study limited to high-level strategic advisory activities. Private partner identities, confidential discussions, detailed system specifications, financial assumptions, and unpublished IP are excluded. Publication should be reviewed with the venture founder.

CONSUMER PRODUCT / GTM STRATEGY & VALIDATION

The Shotmaker’s Game — Bringing a New Golf Format to Market

Helping shape the market introduction of Six/Six Golf through product positioning, audience research, structured testing, and commercialization planning.

01 / POSITIONProduct & Messaging

Explain the six-club, six-ball challenge and what makes the playing experience distinctive.

02 / LEARNAudience Research

Explore golfer needs, likely early adopters, and potential coaching and league use cases.

03 / VALIDATEPhased Testing

Move from concept feedback to practice testing, then a proposed on-course pilot.

04 / PLANCommercial Strategy

Evaluate pricing options, activation metrics, and routes to consumer and partner adoption.

Stage: Product validation & GTM planning

The Challenge

A new golf format must communicate unfamiliar rules without overwhelming players, demonstrate why the experience is worth trying, and establish which audiences would play repeatedly or pay.

The Strategic Approach

Lead with the game experience rather than app features. Define a clear value proposition, explore consumer and coaching/league audiences, and use research to test market interest before scaling a launch.

The Advisory Work

  • Developed positioning and messaging around a creative, constrained style of play.
  • Structured audience personas, competitive positioning, and an initial commercialization framework.
  • Designed a three-stage validation approach: concept review and survey, hands-on demo/practice, and a proposed real-round pilot.
  • Mapped proposed consumer and B2B pricing paths and practical adoption measures including activation and purchase.

Progress & Key Takeaway

The engagement produced a structured GTM framework and phased research plan to guide decisions about positioning, player experience, and commercial options. Commercial performance and broad market adoption have not been established.

Key takeaway: A compelling product concept needs clear positioning and evidence from real users before committing to a growth model.

Public case study of strategic planning and research design. Pricing scenarios and testing plans are exploratory; private tester information, unpublished findings, and internal operating details are not included. Publication should be reviewed with the venture founder.

BUSINESS TRANSFORMATION / GO-TO-MARKET

Building an In-House Digital Media Business

Transforming a largely outsourced operation into a scalable digital media department.

01 / BEFOREOutsourced
OperationsDigital execution primarily handled by outside partners
→
02 / BUILDIn-House
CapabilitiesAd tech selection, hands-on delivery, team, and processes
→
03 / SCALEDigital Media
BusinessRepeatable services and internal delivery capability
400%First-year digital media revenue growth

Compared with a relatively small existing digital media revenue base. Revenue later exceeded $10 million; the reporting period and whether that later figure was annual or cumulative are not specified.

The Challenge

An established advertising agency generated some digital media revenue but relied heavily on external partners for execution. Building internal capabilities offered greater control over delivery and a foundation for growth.

The Strategy

Move core digital media services in-house, beginning with programmatic advertising, paid search, and paid social. Establish the technology, expertise, delivery processes, and management structure required to scale.

The Execution

  • Personally evaluated and selected advertising technology platforms.
  • Initially planned and executed campaigns hands-on across programmatic, paid search, and paid social.
  • Recruited, developed, and managed the digital media team as demand increased.
  • Established campaign operations, workflows, and reporting processes to enable repeatable delivery.

Results & Takeaway

The new internal operation supported 400% first-year digital media revenue growth from a relatively small starting base, and revenue eventually exceeded $10 million. The experience demonstrates how strategy, hands-on implementation, technology selection, and team-building work together to create a scalable business capability.
